newsitem.title: CHINA: China's private economy booming in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China's private economy booming in 1996.

text.p: China's private economy, including private enterprises and individually owned firms, grew rapidly in 1996, the China Business Daily said on Friday.
By the end of 1996, China had 820,000 private enterprises, employing 11.7 million people, up 22.51 percent from the previous year, it said.
Individually owned firms reached 27 million in 1996 and employed 50 million people, a year-on-year increase of 8.75 percent.
The total registered capital of private enterprises amounted to 375.2 billion yuan ($45.2 billion) at the end of last year, soaring 43.13 percent compared with the year before, it said.
Total registered capital of individual firms reached 216.5 billion yuan at the end of 1996, up 19.43 percent compared with 1995.
The total output value of individual firms increased year-on-year by 26.78 percent to 353.9 billion yuan last year, while sales rose 28.77 percent to 1155.3 billion yuan in 1996.
China's burgeoning private business will account for 20.2 percent of the national economy by 2000, state media has said. ($1= 8.3 yuan)
